dedupe_keys.name: a dataset from ten disasters for studying location descriptions and training ai models

description: A dataset from ten disasters for studying location descriptions and training AI models is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Kai Sun et al. People have been increasingly using social media to post messages during a natural disaster, and describe the locations of victims, damages, difficult situations, and relief resources. Many of these location descriptions are in the forms of detailed and multi-entity descriptions, such as door number addresses, road intersections, and highway exits. Coverage: not stated; published in 2026. Formats: JSON, Image, PDF, Python. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 502854258 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
